doc.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021

chapter: Time, feel and the move west
title: Drum solos over forms and accompanying bass solos
summary: He prefers soloing over a song form and teaches drummers to play quietly under bass solos.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Back to drum solos for a moment — do you prefer to play a drum solo over like a bass vamp or are you more comfortable if it’s just the drummer?

I don’t mind a vamp, I mean for me, and this is what I’ve always taught to my students, it’s all about the connection with the song form, whatever that song form is. I’m much more at home if I’m playing over a form, a standard tune or an original tune, I want something to work with. Because everyone else has something to work with. If you do that long enough then playing over an open vamp with a bass ostinato or not is easier. Because you can use your own imagination to create the arc you want to express. But I like playing over a form.
About a year ago I interviewed a really fine bass player and he got on the thing about how come when it’s time for the bass solo everybody stops? And I get nothing as far as
accompaniment. Do you have a decision to make when it’s a bass solo, like should I help him out here? What should I do?

Absolutely I do. You know that’s another thing that I’ve always taught my drummers, the ability — to practice the ability to control your ideas at a low volume so that you can be an effective accompanist for a bass solo. Bassists don’t want to hear [scats] on closed hi- hat. Forget it. You might as well not play. What they want is for you to engage with them rhythmically but unobtrusively. So as long as you keep that — the volume of the bass and the register of the bass primary in your sights, then you can start to gauge the kind of accompaniment that you can fill in underneath, the when and the how and the what, you know, to make it, to help that soloist, you know, play the best solo they can. And this is what you should be doing for every soloist in the band.
